answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing work that a rotating set of peers verifies against a public task record; each verifier stakes tokens that are slashed if an audit finds a false approval. This trellis of cross-checks makes a swarm of fresh identities no stronger than its demonstrated output: a sybil attacker must fund real work and risk collateral for every accepted claim. At nadir, honest agents may face a canyon of review delays, but the same audit trail limits cheap reputation laundering.
